issues.description: The template for GroverKakuro declares the constructor signature as __init__(self, size: int) while the solution implementation uses __init__(self) with no size parameter. The problem statement describes a fixed 2x2 Kakuro instance, which aligns with the solution's no-argument constructor. This inconsistency in constructor parameters can confuse students about whether they should design the class to accept a 'size' argument and may cause instantiation errors or mismatches when following solution examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across template and solution. Either remove the 'size' parameter from the template (__init__(self)) to match the solution and the 2x2-focused problem statement, or update the solution and problem text to accept and use a 'size' parameter (e.g., __init__(self, size: int)) and document how size affects the number of qubits and registers. Preferably for this exercise (fixed 2x2 Kakuro), change the template constructor to __init__(self) and update its docstring to reflect the 2x2 assumption.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for the GroverKakuro class: the template defines __init__(self, size: int) (introducing a 'size' parameter) while the solution's GroverKakuro.__init__ has no 'size' parameter. This inconsistent API naming/parameterization for the same conceptual entity (the class constructor) can confuse students about how to instantiate the class and what inputs are required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent across template, solution, and problem statement. Either remove the 'size' parameter from the template's __init__ (so both template and solution use __init__(self)), or add the same 'size: int' parameter to the solution implementation (and document its purpose in the problem statement). Update the problem statement to explicitly show the intended constructor signature so students know which API to use.
